title: Giftwrapped Army
problem: Each roll can pick a buff the Mimic already has, so it often ends up with fewer buffs than there are Mimics on the side: a repeat just lands on the buff it already has. The text promises one buff per Mimic. The game's other random-buff effects pass the creature receiving the buff, so buffs it already has are skipped; this one passes 'no creature'.
notes: Text: At the start of battle, your {RACE_Mimic} creatures gain a random buff for each {RACE_Mimic} fighting on your side. This trait does not stack. Evidence: bc_StartupBuffsDebuffs L1000 gate scr_AnyAllyHasPassive(1298) @0x1416a593a; L1003 bc_CountRace @0x1416a5d09; L1005 argument -1 (lea 0x1498f7290 = -1.0 @0x1416a5e97, copied by call 0x14028c4a0 @0x1416a5ea1) -> bc_GetRandomBuff @0x1416a5f08; L1006 scr_CritAddCondition @0x1416a639a. bc_GetRandomBuff L18-L22 re-picks while the target already has the buff, but only when its argument is not -1. Fix sketch: Pass the Mimic instead of -1. Redirect the RValue copy at 0x1416a5ea1 to a hook that writes global.crits[i] into the argument slot [rsp+0x140], where i is the loop index used at L1006 (read with the same varget as @0x1416a6020). Reasoning: 'A random buff for each Mimic' promises a count, and repeats quietly reduce it. The game's own usual pattern (bc_GetRandomBuff given the receiver) already avoids repeats, so the fix is one argument. App note (unpatched game): Giftwrapped Army can give a Mimic the same buff more than once, so it may end up with fewer buffs than there are Mimics. Source: errata round 2 (2026-10-26). | Patch (batch L): bc_StartupBuffsDebuffs L1005 bc_GetRandomBuff(-1) @0x1416a5f08 goes to a hook that passes global.crits[i] (i = the loop index at [rsp+0x48], the one the L1006 add uses); bc_GetRandomBuff then re-picks while the creature already has the buff (up to 50 tries).

release_notes.intended: At the start of battle, your Mimic creatures gain a random buff for each Mimic fighting on your side.
release_notes.actual: In the unpatched game, a roll could land on a buff the Mimic already had, so it often ended up with fewer buffs than there are Mimics.
release_notes.fix: Now each roll skips buffs the Mimic already has, as the game's other random-buff effects do.
